quiz.q: If 12 divides a number, which of these must also divide it?
quiz.explain: 4 is a factor of 12, so it divides every multiple of 12. 8, 5 and 24 do not divide 12 itself.
steps: Factors of 12 divide every multiple of 12
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 12 instead of a factor

teach.ask: Gappu's number leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3, and so does Pari's. Without knowing the numbers, what remainder does their sum leave?
teach.praise: 2 + 2 = 4, and 4 leaves 1 when divided by 3. Remainders can be added — magic!
teach.nudge: What do you get if you add the two remainders? Is that bigger than 3?

learn.hook: A riddle: 'Put my pebbles in 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s or 6s and one is always left over; put them in 7s and none are left.' The answer is 301!
points: A number that leaves remainder 1 on division by 2, 3 and 4 is 1 more than a multiple of LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12: 13, 25, 37, ...
Pebble riddle: 1 more than a multiple of LCM(2, 3, 4, 5, 6) = 60, so 61, 121, 181, 241, 301, ... The first one divisible by 7 is 301.
If the remainder is always one less than the divisor (1 for 2, 2 for 3, 3 for 4), then the number + 1 is a common multiple: 11, 23, 35, ...
Nearest multiple of 9: find the remainder with the digit sum. 4567 has digit sum 22 → remainder 4, so 4563 is 4 below and 4572 is 5 above; 4563 is nearest.
Counting multiples in a range: the multiples of 9 from 100 to 200 run from 108 to 198, giving (198 − 108) ÷ 9 + 1 = 11 numbers.

example.q: Find the smallest number that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, and is divisible by 7.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers packing sweets into boxes of different sizes meet these riddles every day!

items.text: Smallest number > 1 with remainder 1 on dividing by 2, 3 and 4: ___

games.title: Pebble riddle steps
items: Remainder 1 for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 → number = multiple of 60 + 1
Test each for division by 7
301 = 7 × 43, so the answer is 301

quiz.q: What is the smallest number greater than 1 that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4 and 5?
quiz.explain: It must be 1 more than a multiple of LCM(2, 3, 4, 5) = 60, so 61.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the remainder, or uses a non-common multiple

quiz.q: Marbles in groups of 3 or 4 leave 1 over; in groups of 5 none are left. What is the smallest number of marbles?
quiz.explain: The number is 1 more than a multiple of 12: 13, 25, 37, ... The first divisible by 5 is 25.
quiz.mistake: Ignores one of the conditions

quiz.q: Which number leaves remainder 1 on ÷ 2, 2 on ÷ 3, 3 on ÷ 4 and 4 on ÷ 5, and is the smallest such number?
quiz.explain: Each remainder is one less than the divisor, so the number + 1 is a multiple of 60. So 60 − 1 = 59.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of subtracting

quiz.q: What is the nearest multiple of 9 to 4567?
quiz.explain: Digit sum 22 → remainder 4. 4567 − 4 = 4563 is 4 away; 4572 is 5 away. So 4563 is nearer.
quiz.mistake: Rounds up without comparing the distances

quiz.q: How many multiples of 9 are there from 100 to 200?
quiz.explain: The first is 108 = 9 × 12 and the last is 198 = 9 × 22. From 12 to 22 there are 11 numbers.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count both ends

quiz.q: How many multiples of 9 are there from 1 to 500?
quiz.mistake: Rounds 500 ÷ 9 ≈ 55.6 up

quiz.q: What is the smallest number you must add to 34,56,789 to get a multiple of 9?
quiz.explain: Digit sum = 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 9 = 42 → remainder 6. Adding 3 makes it a multiple of 9.
quiz.mistake: Gives the remainder instead of what must be added

quiz.q: Amma has between 30 and 50 laddoos. In boxes of 4, 3 are left; in boxes of 6, 5 are left; in boxes of 5, none are left. How many laddoos?
quiz.explain: Remainders 3 and 5 are one less than 4 and 6, so the number + 1 is a multiple of 12: 35 or 47. Only 35 is a multiple of 5.
quiz.mistake: Checks only some of the conditions

teach.ask: Gappu's grandma says: 'In pairs, one seed is left; in threes, one is left; in fours, one is left.' What is the smallest number of seeds (more than 1)?
teach.praise: 13! One more than 12, the LCM of 2, 3 and 4. Grandma will be impressed!
teach.nudge: What number do 2, 3 and 4 all divide? What do you do with the leftover 1?

learn.hook: Can you tell whether 7,35,816 is divisible by 8 without dividing at all? Just peek at the last three digits!
points: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even, by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5, and by 10 if it ends in 0.
Divisible by 4: check the number made by the last two digits. This works because 100 is a multiple of 4.
Divisible by 8: check the number made by the last three digits. This works because 1000 = 8 × 125.
A number divisible by 8 is also divisible by 4 and 2, but a number divisible by 4 need not be divisible by 8 (like 12).
The remainder on dividing by 4 is the same as the remainder for the last two digits: 9,147 → 47 → remainder 3.

example.q: Is 73,512 divisible by 8? Is it divisible by 4?
steps: Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4
example.answer: Yes, it is divisible by both 8 and 4

learn.reallife: Leap years use the rule for 4: the year 2028 is a leap year because 28 is divisible by 4.

games.title: Divisibility detective
items: If a number is divisible by 4, it is divisible by 8.
12 is divisible by 4 but not by 8.
If a number is divisible by 8, it is divisible by 4.
8 = 4 × 2, so every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4.
2,46,000 is divisible by 8.
Its last three digits are 000, and 0 is divisible by 8.
A number ending in 5 can be even.
Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
3,130 is divisible by 4.
The last two digits make 30, and 30 is not a multiple of 4.
Every number divisible by 10 is divisible by both 2 and 5.
10 = 2 × 5, so any multiple of 10 is a multiple of 2 and of 5.

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 4?
quiz.explain: Look at the last two digits: 18, 22, 36 and 10. Only 36 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 9), so 7,236 is divisible by 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even number is divisible by 4

quiz.q: What is the smallest digit that can fill the blank in 52_4 to make it divisible by 8?
quiz.explain: Check the last three digits 2_4. 204 and 214 are not multiples of 8, but 224 = 8 × 28. So the smallest digit is 2.
quiz.mistake: Picks 0 without checking, or looks only at the last two digits

quiz.q: Kabir checks whether 1,236 is divisible by 4. Which reasoning is correct?
options: No, because 6 is not divisible by 4
Yes, because its last two digits make 36, which is divisible by 4
Yes, because its digits add up to 12
quiz.explain: The test for 4 uses the number made by the last two digits. 36 = 4 × 9, so 1,236 is divisible by 4.
quiz.mistake: Uses only the last digit, or uses the digit-sum test that belongs to 3 and 9

quiz.q: How many numbers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 4?
quiz.explain: The multiples of 4 up to 100 are 4, 8, ..., 100. That is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 numbers.
steps: Largest multiple of 4 up to 100 is 100 = 4 × 25
quiz.mistake: Leaves out 100 itself, or counts even numbers instead

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 8?
quiz.explain: Check the last three digits: 108, 324, 220 and 416. Only 416 = 8 × 52 is a multiple of 8.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the last two digits, which is the test for 4

quiz.q: Why does the test for 4 only look at the last two digits?
options: Because 100 is a multiple of 4, so the hundreds and higher places never leave a remainder
Because the last two digits are always the largest
It is just a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: Any number = (hundreds part) + (last two digits). The hundreds part is a multiple of 100 = 4 × 25, so only the last two digits decide.
quiz.mistake: Believes divisibility rules are magic instead of place value

quiz.q: Riya's number is divisible by both 2 and 5. What must its last digit be?
quiz.explain: Divisible by 5 means it ends in 0 or 5. Divisible by 2 means it is even. Only 0 does both.
quiz.mistake: Picks 5, forgetting the number must also be even

quiz.q: What is the remainder when 9,147 is divided by 4?
quiz.explain: The remainder is the same as for the last two digits, 47. 47 = 4 × 11 + 3, so the remainder is 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses only the last digit (7) as the remainder

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I check if 5,732 is divisible by 4 without long division?
teach.praise: The last two digits make 32 = 4 × 8, and 100 is a multiple of 4 anyway. So yes! Easy peasy!
teach.nudge: Which part of the number do you need to look at for 4? Why can we ignore the rest?

learn.hook: Add the digits of 61,875: 6 + 1 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 27. Because 27 is a multiple of 9, so is 61,875. Magic? No, place value!
points: A number is divisible by 3 if its digit sum is divisible by 3, and divisible by 9 if its digit sum is divisible by 9.
Why it works: 10 = 9 + 1, 100 = 99 + 1, 1000 = 999 + 1. So a number and its digit sum leave the same remainder when divided by 9 (or by 3).
Digital root: keep adding the digits until one digit is left. For 9,875: 29 → 11 → 2, so 9,875 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 9.
Divisible by 6: the number must be divisible by both 2 and 3.
Divisible by 11: starting from the right, subtract and add the digits in turn. If the result is 0 or a multiple of 11, so is the number.

example.q: Is 61,875 divisible by 9? Is it divisible by 6?
steps: 61,875 is odd, so it is not divisible by 2
So it is not divisible by 6

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use digit sums to quickly check bills: if the digital roots do not match, there is a mistake somewhere.

items.text: 5_1 is divisible by 9. The missing digit is ___
A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by 2 and by ___

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 9?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number ending in 8 or 9 must be divisible by 9

quiz.q: What is the digital root of 58,463?
quiz.explain: 5 + 8 + 4 + 6 + 3 = 26, and 2 + 6 = 8. The digital root is 8.
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first digit sum (26)

quiz.q: What is the remainder when 1,234 is divided by 9?
quiz.explain: The digit sum is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, and 10 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 9. Check: 9 × 137 = 1233, and 1234 − 1233 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Uses the last digit as the remainder

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 11?
quiz.explain: For 9,152, from the right: 2 − 5 + 1 − 9 = −11, a multiple of 11. Indeed 9,152 = 11 × 832.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the digits, which is the test for 3 and 9

quiz.q: Arjun wants 74_5 to be divisible by 3. Which of these digits can fill the blank?
quiz.explain: Digit sum = 7 + 4 + _ + 5 = 16 + _. With 2 it becomes 18, a multiple of 3. With 3, 4 or 6 it becomes 19, 20 or 22.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to include the fixed digits in the digit sum

quiz.q: Is 2,346 divisible by 6?
options: No, because its digit sum 15 is not divisible by 6
Yes, because it is even and its digit sum 15 is divisible by 3
Yes, only because its last digit is 6
No, because it is not divisible by 3
quiz.explain: 6 = 2 × 3. 2,346 is even, and 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 15 is divisible by 3, so 2,346 is divisible by 6 (2,346 = 6 × 391).
quiz.mistake: Thinks the digit sum must be divisible by 6

quiz.q: Meena says: every number divisible by 3 is also divisible by 9. Which number proves her wrong?
quiz.explain: 12 = 3 × 4 is divisible by 3, but 12 ÷ 9 is not a whole number. The other three are all multiples of 9.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 9, which agrees with Meena instead of proving her wrong

quiz.q: Why does the digit-sum test work for 9?
options: Because 10, 100, 1000, ... are each 1 more than a multiple of 9
quiz.explain: Each 1 ten, 1 hundred or 1 thousand is a multiple of 9 plus 1. So each digit adds just itself to the remainder, and the digit sum gives the same remainder.
quiz.mistake: Links the rule to 9 being a big digit instead of to place value

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I find out whether 4,518 is divisible by 9 without dividing?
teach.praise: Add the digits: 4 + 5 + 1 + 8 = 18, a multiple of 9, so 4,518 is too. That is a cool shortcut!
teach.nudge: What should you do with the digits 4, 5, 1 and 8? Then what do you check?

learn.hook: EF × E = GGG. Three letters, one multiplication, and only one answer. Can you crack the code?
points: In letter puzzles, each letter is a digit. Use place value, last digits, parity and divisibility. GGG = G × 111 = G × 3 × 37, so EF × E = GGG means EF = 37 and E = 3: 37 × 3 = 111.
Place value helps: AB + BA = (10A + B) + (10B + A) = 11(A + B). So AB + BA = 121 means A + B = 11.
Products of consecutive whole numbers: two in a row is always divisible by 2; three in a row by 6; four in a row by 24.

Venn diagrams of multiples: every multiple of 32 is a multiple of 8, and every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4 — the circles sit inside each other. Multiples of 4 and of 6 overlap in the multiples of 12.

example.q: Solve EF × E = GGG.
steps: EF is a two-digit factor, so EF = 37 (or 74, which fails)

learn.reallife: Codes on lockers and puzzles in newspapers use exactly these tricks.

games.title: Where do they sit in the Venn diagram?
Consecutive products
items: 4 × 5 is divisible by 2.
One of two consecutive numbers is even.
7 × 8 × 9 is divisible by 6.
Every product of 3 consecutive numbers is divisible by 24.
3 × 4 × 5 × 6 is divisible by 24.

quiz.q: In EF × E = GGG, what two-digit number is EF?
quiz.explain: GGG = G × 3 × 37. The two-digit number EF must be 37 with E = 3, since 37 × 3 = 111.
quiz.mistake: Tries 11, which repeats digits

quiz.q: AB + BA = 132 for digits A and B. What is A + B?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 11

quiz.q: The product of any 3 consecutive whole numbers is always divisible by which number?
quiz.explain: Among 3 consecutive numbers, one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so the product is divisible by 6.
steps: Always a multiple of 2 and of 3
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that fails for 1 × 2 × 3

quiz.q: The product of any 4 consecutive whole numbers is always divisible by which number?
quiz.explain: 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 24, and every such product contains a multiple of 4, another even number and a multiple of 3.
steps: Includes a multiple of 4, another even, and a multiple of 3
quiz.mistake: Stops at 12

quiz.q: Is every multiple of 32 also a multiple of 8?
quiz.explain: 32 is a multiple of 8, so every multiple of 32 is a multiple of 8. In a Venn diagram the 32-circle sits inside the 8-circle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which set is inside which

quiz.q: Which number is a multiple of 8 but NOT a multiple of 32?
quiz.explain: 40 = 8 × 5 but 40 ÷ 32 is not whole. 64 and 96 are multiples of 32; 20 is not a multiple of 8.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 32

quiz.q: A two-digit number AB equals 4 times the sum of its digits. If A = 3, what is AB?
quiz.mistake: Guesses without using place value

quiz.q: What is 5 × 6 × 7 × 8 divided by 24?
quiz.explain: 5 × 6 × 7 × 8 = 1680, and 1680 ÷ 24 = 70. (Four consecutive numbers always give a multiple of 24.)
quiz.mistake: Slips in the multiplication

teach.ask: Gappu found the puzzle AB + BA = 99 and has no idea where to start. Teach him!
teach.praise: AB + BA = 11(A + B) = 99, so A + B = 9! Place value is the key to the code.
teach.nudge: What is AB worth in terms of A and B? Try writing it as 10A + B.

learn.hook: You know 23 × 17 = 391. What is 24 × 17? Don't start again — just add one more 17!
points: If one factor goes up by 1, the product goes up by the other factor: (a + 1) × b = ab + b. So 24 × 17 = 391 + 17 = 408.
If both factors go up by 1: (a + 1)(b + 1) = ab + a + b + 1.
To keep a product the same, multiply one factor by a number and divide the other by the same number: 12 × 18 = 24 × 9 = 6 × 36 = 216.
Comparing 14 × 26 and 16 × 24: both pairs add to 40. 14 × 26 = (20 − 6)(20 + 6) = 400 − 36 = 364 and 16 × 24 = 400 − 16 = 384. The closer the two numbers, the bigger the product.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers adjust bills quickly this way: if 12 items cost ₹420 at ₹35 each, one more item just adds ₹35.

quiz.explain: Increasing 23 by 1 adds one more 17: 391 + 17 = 408.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of adding the other factor

quiz.explain: Increasing 12 by 1 adds one more 35: 420 + 35 = 455.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong factor (12 instead of 35)

quiz.q: 10 × 20 becomes 11 × 21. By how much does the product increase?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra 1 × 1

quiz.q: Which product equals 12 × 18?
quiz.explain: Doubling 12 and halving 18 keeps the product: 24 × 9 = 216. The others are 221, 224 and 108.
quiz.mistake: Adds and subtracts the same amount instead of multiplying and dividing

quiz.q: Which is larger, 14 × 26 or 16 × 24?
options: It cannot be told without a calculator
quiz.explain: Both pairs add to 40. 14 × 26 = 400 − 36 = 364 and 16 × 24 = 400 − 16 = 384. The closer pair gives the bigger product.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal sums give equal products
Assumes the two products are equal

quiz.q: In a × b, a is multiplied by 3. What must happen to b to keep the product the same?
quiz.explain: (3a) × (b ÷ 3) = ab. Multiplying by 3 must be undone by dividing by 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks subtracting 3 balances multiplying by 3

quiz.q: Rahul doubles 25 and halves 48 in 25 × 48. What is the product now?
quiz.explain: Doubling one factor and halving the other keeps the product: 50 × 24 = 1200 = 25 × 48.
quiz.mistake: Thinks doubling makes the product double

teach.ask: Gappu knows 40 × 15 = 600. He needs 41 × 15 fast. What should he do?
teach.praise: Just add one more 15: 615! No need to multiply all over again.
teach.nudge: If 40 becomes 41, how many extra 15s do you get?

learn.hook: Can you work out 7 × 102 in your head in two seconds? Split 102 into 100 + 2, and it is 700 + 14 = 714!
points: Distributive property: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. For example, 6 × 47 = 6 × 40 + 6 × 7 = 240 + 42 = 282.
It works with subtraction too: a × (b − c) = a × b − a × c. So 8 × 99 = 800 − 8 = 792.
Area picture: a rectangle a wide and (b + c) long splits into two rectangles with areas ab and ac.
Two brackets: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd. Every term in the first bracket multiplies every term in the second.
It works for algebra: 3x(2x + 5) = 6x² + 15x.

example.q: Find 23 × 14 by splitting both numbers.

learn.reallife: A shopkeeper selling 6 kurtas at ₹499 each thinks 6 × 500 − 6 × 1 = ₹3000 − ₹6 = ₹2994. Quick and correct!

quiz.q: Simplify 5(2x + 3).
quiz.explain: Multiply 5 with each term inside: 5 × 2x = 10x and 5 × 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first term inside the bracket

quiz.q: What is 8 × 99, using the distributive property?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Expand (x + 3)(x + 4).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only first × first and last × last, missing the middle terms

quiz.q: Riya buys 6 pens at ₹47 each. She works it out as 6 × 40 + 6 × 7. How much does she pay?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the tens part by 6 and adds 7

quiz.q: Expand 3a(a − 2b).
quiz.explain: 3a × a = 3a² and 3a × 2b = 6ab, keeping the minus sign: 3a² − 6ab.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the second term by 3a, or loses the minus sign

quiz.q: A garden is 9 m wide and (10 + 2) m long. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 9 by 10 only and then adds 2

quiz.q: Expand (2x + 1)(x − 3).
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign slip when combining −6x and x

quiz.q: When expanding (a + b)(c + d), how many products do you write before combining like terms?
quiz.explain: Each of the 2 terms in the first bracket multiplies each of the 2 terms in the second: 2 × 2 = 4 products (ac, ad, bc, bd).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only matching terms, giving just 2 products

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I multiply 4 × (x + 3)? Is it 4x + 3?
teach.praise: The 4 must multiply each term inside: 4 × x and 4 × 3, so 4x + 12. Got it!
teach.nudge: Does the 4 multiply only the x, or every term inside the bracket?

learn.hook: Multiplying (x² + 2x + 3) by (x + 1) looks scary. Put it in a grid and it becomes a simple fill-in-the-boxes game!
points: Grid method: write the terms of one bracket along the top and the other down the side. Fill each box with a product, then add all the boxes and combine like terms.
A trinomial times a binomial gives 3 × 2 = 6 products: (x² + 2x + 3)(x + 1) = x³ + x² + 2x² + 2x + 3x + 3 = x³ + 3x² + 5x + 3.
A beautiful pattern: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b², (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) = a³ − b³, (a − b)(a³ + a²b + ab² + b³) = a⁴ − b⁴. All the middle terms cancel.

example.q: Use a grid to expand (2x + 3)(x + 4).

learn.reallife: Engineers expand long products when they work out areas and volumes of boxes whose sides change.

quiz.q: How many products are written when expanding (a + b + c)(d + e)?
quiz.explain: Each of the 3 terms meets each of the 2 terms: 3 × 2 = 6 products.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers of terms instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Expand (x² + 2x + 3)(x + 1).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first terms and the last terms

quiz.q: Expand (x + 2)(x² − 2x + 4).
quiz.explain: x³ − 2x² + 4x + 2x² − 4x + 8 = x³ + 8. The middle terms cancel.
quiz.mistake: Misses the cancelling terms

quiz.q: What is (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)?
quiz.explain: a³ + a²b + ab² − a²b − ab² − b³ = a³ − b³.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with (a − b)³
Forgets to subtract the 1

quiz.q: In the grid for (2x + 3)(x + 4), what goes in the box for 3 × 4?
quiz.explain: Each box holds a product: 3 × 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying in the box
Gives 2⁴ instead of 2⁴ − 1

quiz.q: What is the coefficient of x² in (x² + x + 1)(x + 2)?
quiz.explain: x² comes from x² × 2 and x × x: 2x² + x² = 3x².
quiz.mistake: Counts only one of the two x² terms

teach.ask: Gappu must expand (x + 1)(x² + x + 1) and keeps losing terms. How can a grid help?
teach.praise: Two rows, three columns, six boxes — then add the like terms. I didn't lose a single term!
teach.nudge: How many boxes does the grid need? What do you do after filling them?

learn.hook: Is (a + b)² the same as a² + b²? Try a = 1 and b = 1: (1 + 1)² = 4 but 1² + 1² = 2. Something is missing!
points: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². In a square of side (a + b), there are two a × b rectangles besides the squares a² and b².
(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
An identity is true for every value of the letters, unlike an equation such as x + 3 = 7, which is true for only one value.

example.q: Find 51² using an identity.

learn.reallife: Builders use (a + b)² when a square courtyard of side a is made b metres longer and b metres wider: the new area is a² + 2ab + b².

games.title: Identity or imposter?
items: (a + b)² = a² + b² for all numbers a and b.
With a = b = 1, the left side is 4 and the right side is 2. The 2ab term is missing.
(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² with a = x, b = 3.
(a − b)² = (b − a)²
b − a is the negative of a − b, and a number and its negative have the same square.
(m + n)² − (m − n)² = 4mn
(m² + 2mn + n²) − (m² − 2mn + n²) = 4mn.
(2x)² = 2x²

quiz.q: Expand (x + 6)².
quiz.mistake: Squares each term and forgets the middle term 2ab

quiz.q: Use (a + b)² to find 21².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 2ab term and gets 401

quiz.q: What is 98²?
quiz.mistake: Writes 100² − 2² (9996), forgetting the middle term

quiz.q: Expand (3y − 2)².
quiz.mistake: Writes 3y² instead of squaring the 3 as well

quiz.q: If a + b = 7 and ab = 10, what is a² + b²?
quiz.explain: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, so a² + b² = 49 − 20 = 29. (Check: a = 5, b = 2 gives 25 + 4 = 29.)
quiz.mistake: Adds 2ab instead of subtracting it (gets 69)

quiz.q: Kabir's square plot has side (x + 2) m. Which expression gives its area in m²?
quiz.mistake: Writes the perimeter 4x + 8, or forgets the middle term

quiz.q: What is 105²?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 × 5 instead of 2 × 100 × 5 for the middle term (gets 10,525)

quiz.q: Harpreet tests the rule with a = 3 and b = 4. What is (3 + 4)²?
quiz.explain: (3 + 4)² = 7² = 49. Note that 3² + 4² = 25, which is different, so (a + b)² is not a² + b². The missing part is 2ab = 24.
quiz.mistake: Squares each number separately and adds (gets 25)

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: (a + b)² is just a² + b², right? Square both and add!
teach.praise: Oh! The square of side a + b has two a × b rectangles too, so (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². I was missing a piece!
teach.nudge: Draw a square of side a + b. Besides a² and b², what other pieces are inside it?

topics.title: Difference of squares and quick products

learn.hook: 52 × 48 looks hard, but 52 and 48 are 2 more and 2 less than 50. So it is just 50² − 2² = 2496!
points: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². The middle terms +ab and −ab cancel out.
Difference of squares the other way: 47² − 43² = (47 + 43)(47 − 43) = 90 × 4 = 360.
Picture: from an a × a square, cut off a b × b corner. The leftover pieces rearrange into a rectangle (a + b) by (a − b).

example.q: Find 103 × 97 quickly.

learn.reallife: Mental-maths champions use (a + b)(a − b) to multiply numbers like 61 × 59 = 3600 − 1 = 3599 in a flash.

games.title: Identity or not?
items: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
a(b + c) = ab + ac
(a + b)² = a² + b²
(a − b)² = a² − b²

quiz.q: What is 41 × 39, using (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²?
quiz.mistake: Adds b² instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Find 47² − 43² without squaring either number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a² − b² = (a − b)², which gives 16

quiz.q: Expand (x + 5)(x − 5).
quiz.explain: This is (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² with a = x and b = 5, so the answer is x² − 25.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of 25 wrong

quiz.q: Expand (x + 3)(x + 7).
quiz.explain: (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab = x² + 10x + 21.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the sum and the product

quiz.q: Meena's square rangoli has side 25 cm. She cuts a 5 cm square out of one corner. What area is left?
quiz.mistake: Uses (25 − 5)² = 400 instead of 25² − 5²

quiz.q: What is 999 × 1001?
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of subtracting, or rounds to 1000²

quiz.q: Which product equals x² − 9?
quiz.explain: (x + 3)(x − 3) = x² − 3² = x² − 9. (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, which has a middle term.
quiz.mistake: Thinks (x − 3)² equals x² − 9

quiz.q: (x + 4)(x − 2) = x² + px − 8. What is p?
quiz.explain: The x-term is (4 + (−2))x = 2x, so p = 2. Check the constant: 4 × (−2) = −8.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the minus sign and adds 4 + 2 = 6

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I find 52 × 48 in my head? It looks too hard!
teach.praise: 52 and 48 are 50 plus 2 and 50 minus 2, so 50² − 2² = 2500 − 4 = 2496. Wow, magic maths!
teach.nudge: Which number is exactly in the middle of 52 and 48? How far is each number from it?

topics.title: Differences of squares and growing patterns

learn.hook: Can every number be written as one square minus another? 15 = 8² − 7² and 24 = 7² − 5². But try 6 — you will never manage!
points: Every odd number is a difference of two consecutive squares: 2k + 1 = (k + 1)² − k². So 15 = 8² − 7².

Every multiple of 4 is a difference of squares too: 4k = (k + 1)² − (k − 1)². So 24 = 7² − 5². Numbers like 2, 6, 10, 14 (2 more than a multiple of 4) can never be written this way using whole numbers.
An identity must work for every number — negatives and fractions too. Test (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² with a = −3, b = 5: both sides give 4.
Growing patterns: a row of y squares made of matchsticks needs 3y + 1 sticks. The border of tiles around a y × y square uses (y + 2)² − y² = 4y + 4 tiles.

example.q: Write 40 as a difference of two squares.

learn.reallife: Tile layers and fence posts follow growing patterns — builders use rules like 4y + 4 to order materials.

items.q: Matchsticks for 10 squares in a row (3y + 1)

quiz.q: How can 15 be written as a difference of two consecutive squares?
quiz.mistake: Uses squares that are not consecutive or gives a different number

quiz.q: Which of these equals 24?
quiz.mistake: Picks squares that differ by the wrong amount

quiz.q: Which number can NOT be written as a difference of two squares of whole numbers?
quiz.explain: 6 is 2 more than a multiple of 4, and such numbers are never a difference of two squares. 9 = 5² − 4², 8 = 3² − 1², 15 = 8² − 7².
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even number fails

quiz.q: With a = −3 and b = 5, what is a² + 2ab + b²?
quiz.explain: 9 + 2(−3)(5) + 25 = 9 − 30 + 25 = 4, which equals (a + b)² = 2² = 4. The identity works for negatives too.
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign error with 2ab

quiz.q: With a = 1/2 and b = 1/3, what is a² − b²?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the fractions before squaring

quiz.q: A row of y squares made of matchsticks needs 3y + 1 sticks. How many sticks make 10 squares?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the first extra stick

quiz.q: How many tiles form a one-tile border around a 6 × 6 square?
quiz.mistake: Counts 4 × 6 and forgets the 4 corners

quiz.q: A pattern has 2, 6, 12, 20, ... dots, where step y has y(y + 1) dots. How many dots are in step 7?
quiz.mistake: Uses y² instead of y(y + 1)

teach.ask: Gappu tried to write 10 as one square minus another and failed. Is he just unlucky?
teach.praise: Not unlucky! Numbers that are 2 more than a multiple of 4 can never be a difference of squares.
teach.nudge: Which numbers always work? Is 10 odd? Is it a multiple of 4?

topics.title: Mind the mistake, mend the mistake

learn.hook: Raju wrote (x + 4)² = x² + 16 and got a big red cross. What went wrong? Let's become algebra doctors and fix the mistakes!
points: (a + b)² is NOT a² + b². The middle term 2ab is missing: (x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16.
(a − b)² is NOT a² − b²: (x − 5)² = x² − 10x + 25.
A minus sign before a bracket changes every sign inside: 5 − (x − 2) = 5 − x + 2 = 7 − x.
Multiply every term inside: 3(a + 4) = 3a + 12, not 3a + 4. And (2y)² = 4y², not 2y².
Only like terms combine: 4x + 3y stays as it is — it is not 7xy. A quick test with numbers catches most mistakes.

example.q: Raju says (a + b)² = a² + b². Test with a = 2, b = 3.
steps: So the correct rule is a² + 2ab + b²
example.answer: Raju is wrong: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

learn.reallife: Checking answers by putting in simple numbers is what good engineers and accountants do every day.

games.title: Correct or a mistake?
items: (3x)² = 9x²
(a + b)² = a² + b²
3x + 2y = 5xy
x × x = 2x

quiz.q: Raju wrote (x + 4)² = x² + 16. What is the correct expansion?
quiz.explain: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so (x + 4)² = x² + 2 × 4 × x + 16 = x² + 8x + 16.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the middle term 2ab

quiz.q: Simplify 5 − (x − 2) correctly.
quiz.explain: The minus changes both signs inside: 5 − x + 2 = 7 − x.
quiz.mistake: Changes only the first sign inside the bracket

quiz.q: What is (2y)²?
quiz.explain: (2y)² = 2y × 2y = 4y². Both the 2 and the y are squared.
quiz.mistake: Squares only the letter

quiz.q: Kavi wrote 3(a + 4) = 3a + 4. What should it be?
quiz.explain: The 3 multiplies every term inside: 3 × a + 3 × 4 = 3a + 12.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first term in the bracket

quiz.q: Isha simplified 4x + 3y to 7xy. What is correct?
quiz.explain: 4x and 3y are unlike terms, so they cannot be added into one term.
quiz.mistake: Adds unlike terms

quiz.q: Correct the mistake (x − 5)² = x² − 25.
quiz.explain: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²: x² − 10x + 25.
quiz.mistake: Squares each term separately

quiz.q: Tanu wrote (x + 1)(x + 2) = x² + 2. What is correct?
quiz.explain: x·x + 2x + x + 2 = x² + 3x + 2. Each term must multiply each term.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only first × first and last × last

quiz.q: Meena tests the rule (a + b)² = a² + b² with a = 2 and b = 3. By how much do the two sides differ?
quiz.explain: (2 + 3)² = 25 but 2² + 3² = 13. The difference 12 is exactly the missing 2ab = 2 × 2 × 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rule might still be right

teach.ask: Gappu wrote (y + 3)² = y² + 9. He is very proud. Can you gently tell him what went wrong?
teach.praise: Oops! I forgot the middle term 6y. (y + 3)² = y² + 6y + 9. Thanks, doctor!
teach.nudge: What happens if you put y = 1 into both sides? Which term did Gappu forget?

learn.hook: Two friends find the area of the same L-shaped room. One adds, the other subtracts. Different methods — but the answers must match!
points: A shaded area can be found by adding pieces, or by subtracting from a bigger shape. The answers are equal, so the two expressions are equivalent.
L-shape from a big square of side a with a b × b corner cut out: area a² − b². Cut it into two rectangles instead: (a + b)(a − b). So a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
Path outside a plot: (outer rectangle) − (plot). A plot l by w with a path of width p all round has path area (l + 2p)(w + 2p) − lw.
For a square plot of side a with a path of width p outside: (a + 2p)² − a² = 4ap + 4p².
Two expressions are equivalent if they simplify to the same thing, like x(x + 5) + 3x and x² + 8x.

example.q: A garden 20 m by 12 m has a 2 m wide path all round outside it. Find the path's area.

learn.reallife: Builders calculate paths around parks and borders around swimming pools exactly this way.

items.q: Square plot 10 m, path 2 m outside

quiz.q: A plot 30 m by 20 m has a 1 m wide path all round outside it. What is the area of the path?
quiz.explain: Outer rectangle 32 × 22 = 704 m². Path = 704 − 600 = 104 m².
quiz.mistake: Adds the path width only once to each side

quiz.q: A square plot of side 10 m has a 2 m wide path outside it. What is the area of the path?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the four corner squares

quiz.q: A square plot of side a has a 1 m wide path outside it. Which expression gives the path's area?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the corner squares of the path

quiz.q: A 4 cm × 4 cm square is cut from the corner of a 12 cm × 12 cm square. What area is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the side lengths instead of the areas

quiz.q: Ravi writes a shaded area as x(x + 5) + 3x; Sita writes x² + 8x. Who is right?
quiz.explain: x(x + 5) + 3x = x² + 5x + 3x = x² + 8x. Equivalent expressions describe the same area.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one method can be correct

quiz.q: A photo frame has outer size 10 cm × 8 cm and the picture is 6 cm × 4 cm. What is the area of the frame?
quiz.mistake: Gives only the inner or only the outer area

quiz.q: An L-shape is a big square of side a with a b × b corner removed. Cut into two rectangles, which expression gives its area?
quiz.explain: Rearranged, the two rectangles make one rectangle (a + b) long and (a − b) wide, so a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
quiz.mistake: Confuses the L-shape with a smaller square

quiz.q: Two 2 m wide paths cross through the middle of a 30 m × 20 m field, one along its length and one along its width. What is their total area?
quiz.explain: 2 × 30 + 2 × 20 = 100 m², but the 2 × 2 crossing square is counted twice, so 100 − 4 = 96 m².
quiz.mistake: Counts the crossing square twice

teach.ask: Gappu's nest has a square base of side a, with a straw border 1 unit wide all around outside. How can he find the border's area?
teach.praise: Big square minus small square: (a + 2)² − a² = 4a + 4. My border is ready!
teach.nudge: What is the side of the big outer square? What do you take away?

learn.hook: Circle any 2 × 2 block of dates on a calendar. Multiply across the diagonals and subtract. You will ALWAYS get 7. Why?
points: Calendar trick: a 2 × 2 block has dates a, a + 1 (top) and a + 7, a + 8 (below). (a + 1)(a + 7) − a(a + 8) = a² + 8a + 7 − a² − 8a = 7. Always 7!
Middle-square trick: for three consecutive numbers, the middle one squared is 1 more than the product of the other two: n² − (n − 1)(n + 1) = 1. So 24² − 23 × 25 = 1.
Proving statements: (k + 1)(k + 2) − (k + 3) = k² + 2k − 1 = (k + 1)² − 2. So it is always 2 less than a perfect square.
Remainders on division by 7: if a leaves 3 and b leaves 5, then a + b leaves 3 + 5 = 8 → 1, and a × b leaves 3 × 5 = 15 → 1.

example.q: Check the calendar trick on the block 12, 13 / 19, 20.
steps: Algebra shows it is 7 for every block

learn.reallife: Magicians use such provable tricks; mathematicians enjoy showing exactly why they never fail.

games.title: Proved or not?
items: The calendar 2 × 2 diagonal difference is always 7.
n² − (n − 1)(n + 1) = 1 for every n.
(k + 1)(k + 2) − (k + 3) is always a perfect square.
It is always 2 less than a perfect square.
If a leaves 3 and b leaves 5 on division by 7, a + b leaves 8.
8 is more than 7; the remainder is 1.

quiz.q: A calendar block has 12, 13 on top and 19, 20 below. What is 13 × 19 − 12 × 20?
quiz.explain: 13 × 19 = 247 and 12 × 20 = 240. The difference is 7, as the algebra predicts.
quiz.mistake: Expects the two products to be equal

quiz.q: Why is the calendar 2 × 2 diagonal difference always 7?
options: Because a week has 7 days, so any answer is 7
Because the dates are all odd
quiz.explain: a² + 8a + 7 − (a² + 8a) = 7. The 7 comes from 1 × 7 in the expansion.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason without algebra

quiz.q: What is 24² − 23 × 25?
quiz.mistake: Assumes the two are equal

quiz.explain: For consecutive numbers, the middle square is 1 more than the product of its neighbours.
quiz.mistake: Tries to multiply huge numbers and slips

quiz.q: For k = 5, what is (k + 1)(k + 2) − (k + 3)?
quiz.explain: 6 × 7 − 8 = 42 − 8 = 34, which is 6² − 2, as the identity (k + 1)² − 2 says.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract (k + 3)

quiz.q: (k + 1)(k + 2) − (k + 3) is always...
quiz.explain: It simplifies to k² + 2k − 1 = (k + 1)² − 2.
quiz.mistake: Tests one value and guesses a pattern

quiz.q: a leaves remainder 3 and b leaves remainder 5 when divided by 7. What remainder does a × b leave?
quiz.explain: 3 × 5 = 15 = 2 × 7 + 1, so the remainder is 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to reduce 15

quiz.q: a leaves remainder 4 and b leaves remainder 6 when divided by 7. What remainder does a + b leave?
quiz.explain: 4 + 6 = 10 = 7 + 3, so the remainder is 3.
quiz.mistake: Stops at 10, which is not a remainder for 7

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the calendar trick is luck. Can you prove it always gives 7?
teach.praise: With a, a + 1, a + 7 and a + 8, the algebra leaves just 7. Not luck — proof!
teach.nudge: What are the four dates if the top-left one is a?

learn.hook: Stretch a selfie by adding 4 cm to both its width and height, and your face looks squashed. Multiply both by 2, and it looks perfect. Why?
points: Two pictures look alike when the width and height are both multiplied by the same number. A 4 cm × 6 cm photo enlarged to 8 cm × 12 cm (both × 2) keeps its shape.
Adding the same amount to both sides distorts the picture: 4 × 6 becomes 8 × 10 when 4 is added, and the ratio changes from 2 : 3 to 4 : 5.
Quantities are proportional when they change by the same multiplying factor.
Ages show this well: Ravi is 5 and his father is 30 (1 : 6). After 5 years they are 10 and 35, which is 2 : 7 — not 1 : 6. Adding the same number of years changes the ratio.

example.q: A 3 cm × 5 cm photo is enlarged without distortion so its width is 9 cm. What is its height?

learn.reallife: Phone screens and TV screens are sold in fixed shapes such as 16 : 9 so pictures never look stretched.

games.title: Multiply or add?
items: Multiplying width and height by 3 keeps a picture's shape.
Both change by the same factor.
Adding 2 cm to both sides keeps a picture's shape.
6 × 4 becomes 8 × 6, and 3 : 2 is not 4 : 3.
The ratio of two people's ages stays the same every year.
Adding the same years changes the ratio.
A 2 : 3 rectangle and a 10 : 15 rectangle have the same shape.
10 : 15 simplifies to 2 : 3.

quiz.q: A 3 cm × 5 cm photo is enlarged without distortion so its width is 9 cm. What is its new height?
quiz.explain: The width is multiplied by 3, so the height is too: 5 × 3 = 15 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 cm to the height because 6 cm was added to the width

quiz.q: Which change keeps a picture from looking stretched?
options: Add 3 cm to both the width and the height
Add 3 cm to the width only
Multiply the width by 3 and the height by 2
Multiply both the width and the height by 3
quiz.explain: Only the same multiplying factor on both sides keeps the shape.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding the same amount is fair to both sides

quiz.q: A 6 cm × 4 cm picture has 2 cm added to each side. What is the new ratio of width to height?
quiz.explain: It becomes 8 × 6, and 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. The old ratio was 3 : 2, so the picture is distorted.
quiz.mistake: Assumes adding keeps the ratio

quiz.q: Meera is 8 and her mother is 32. What will the ratio of their ages be in 8 years?
quiz.explain: In 8 years they will be 16 and 40, and 16 : 40 = 2 : 5. The ratio 1 : 4 does not stay.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the old ratio

quiz.q: A son is 10 and his father is 30. What will the ratio of their ages be in 10 years?
quiz.explain: They will be 20 and 40, and 20 : 40 = 1 : 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the ratio never changes

quiz.q: A 10 cm × 4 cm card is enlarged in proportion so its width is 25 cm. What is its new height?
quiz.explain: 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5, so the height becomes 4 × 2.5 = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 15 cm to the height as well

quiz.q: Is a 12 cm × 18 cm photo the same shape as a 16 cm × 22 cm photo?
options: Yes — 4 cm was added to both
quiz.explain: Same shape needs equal ratios. 2 : 3 is not equal to 8 : 11, so the shapes differ.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding the same amount keeps the shape

quiz.q: A recipe for 4 uses 2 cups of rice and 3 cups of water. For 12 people, how many cups of water are needed?
quiz.explain: 4 people → 12 people is × 3, so water is 3 × 3 = 9 cups.
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 to match the 8 extra people

teach.ask: Gappu made his photo bigger by adding 5 cm to each side, but now he looks squashed. What went wrong?
teach.praise: I should multiply both sides by the same number, not add! Then I'll keep my handsome shape.
teach.nudge: Did Gappu multiply or add? What keeps the shape the same?

learn.hook: Nimbu pani tastes perfect with 1 spoon of sugar for every 2 glasses of water. For 6 glasses you need 3 spoons. That is a ratio at work!
points: A ratio a : b compares two quantities of the same kind by division. 12 boys and 18 girls give 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.
Use the same unit before writing a ratio: 50 cm : 2 m = 50 cm : 200 cm = 1 : 4.
Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both terms by the same non-zero number: 2 : 3 = 4 : 6 = 10 : 15.
Order matters: 2 : 3 is not the same as 3 : 2.
Part-to-whole: if boys : girls = 2 : 3, then boys are 2 out of every 5 children, that is 2/5 of the class.

example.q: Write 45 minutes : 2 hours in simplest form.
steps: Change to the same unit: 2 hours = 120 minutes

learn.reallife: Recipes, mixing cement and sand, and the 3 : 2 shape of the Indian flag all use ratios.

games.title: Ratio riddles
items: 2 : 3 and 3 : 2 are the same ratio.
Order matters. 2 : 3 means the first is smaller; 3 : 2 means the first is bigger.
4 : 6 and 10 : 15 are equivalent ratios.
Both simplify to 2 : 3.
Change to the same unit first: 100 cm : 50 cm = 2 : 1.
If boys : girls = 3 : 5, then 3/8 of the class are boys.
Out of every 3 + 5 = 8 children, 3 are boys.
Adding the same number to both terms keeps a ratio the same.
1 : 2 becomes 2 : 3 after adding 1, and 1/2 is not equal to 2/3.
Once both quantities are in the same unit, a ratio has no unit.
The units cancel when we divide, e.g. 50 cm ÷ 200 cm = 1/4.

quiz.q: A class has 12 boys and 18 girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 12 : 18. Divide both by their HCF 6 to get 2 : 3.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the order, or does not divide by the HCF fully (6 : 9)

quiz.q: What is the ratio of 50 cm to 2 m?
quiz.explain: Change 2 m to 200 cm. Then 50 : 200 = 1 : 4.
quiz.mistake: Compares the numbers 50 and 2 without changing to the same unit

quiz.q: Arjun cooks rice with 2 cups of rice to 3 cups of water. Which ratio is equivalent to 2 : 3?
quiz.explain: Multiply both terms of 2 : 3 by 4 to get 8 : 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds the same number to both terms (2 + 2 : 3 + 2 = 4 : 5)

quiz.q: In a class of 40, the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. How many girls are there?
quiz.explain: There are 3 + 5 = 8 parts. Each part is 40 ÷ 8 = 5 children, so girls = 5 × 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Finds the number of boys (15) instead of girls

quiz.q: Find x if 4 : 7 = x : 35.
quiz.explain: 7 was multiplied by 5 to get 35, so multiply 4 by 5 too: x = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 28 to 4 (because 7 + 28 = 35) instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Write 45 minutes : 1.5 hours in simplest form.
quiz.explain: 1.5 hours = 90 minutes. 45 : 90 = 1 : 2.
quiz.mistake: Mixes units, or reverses the ratio

quiz.q: In a cricket match Harpreet scored 48 runs and Joseph scored 36 runs. What fraction of their total runs did Harpreet score?
quiz.explain: Total = 48 + 36 = 84. Harpreet's share = 48/84 = 4/7.
quiz.mistake: Writes the part-to-part ratio 48/36 = 4/3 instead of part-to-whole

quiz.q: Riya adds 1 to both terms of 1 : 2 and gets 2 : 3. Is the new ratio equivalent to the old one?
options: Yes, adding the same number keeps ratios equal
Yes, because both ratios grew by 1
quiz.explain: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing, not adding. 1/2 and 2/3 are different values.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding the same amount to both terms keeps the ratio the same

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I know if 4 : 6 and 10 : 15 are the same ratio?
teach.praise: Divide both terms of each ratio by the same number, and both become 2 : 3. They are equivalent!
teach.nudge: What do you get if you simplify each ratio? What must you do to both terms?

learn.hook: On a map, Delhi to Agra is just 4 cm, but the real road is about 200 km long. Maps work because distances are in proportion!
points: Four numbers are in proportion when a : b = c : d. We write a : b :: c : d.
Cross-multiplication test: a : b :: c : d exactly when a × d = b × c. (Product of extremes = product of means.)
To find a missing term: 3 : 4 :: 12 : x means 3x = 4 × 12 = 48, so x = 16.
Proportion uses multiplication, not addition. Going from 3 to 12 is ×4, so 4 becomes 16 (not 4 + 9 = 13).
A map scale of 1 : 50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm = 500 m on the ground.

example.q: Meena makes 12 laddoos with 2 cups of besan. How much besan does she need for 30 laddoos?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers, cooks, map readers and photo editors all scale things up and down in proportion.

items.text: If a : b :: c : d, then a × d = ___

quiz.q: Are 6, 9, 10, 15 in proportion (6 : 9 :: 10 : 15)?
options: No, because 9 − 6 is not equal to 15 − 10
No, because 10 is not a multiple of 6
Only if they are in rupees
quiz.explain: Product of extremes 6 × 15 = 90 equals product of means 9 × 10 = 90, so they are in proportion. Both ratios equal 2 : 3.
quiz.mistake: Compares differences instead of ratios

quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56, so multiply 5 by 7 too: x = 35. Check: 5 × 56 = 280 = 8 × 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds 48 to 5 because 8 + 48 = 56

quiz.q: Meena uses 2 cups of besan for 12 laddoos. How many cups does she need for 30 laddoos?
quiz.explain: 2 : 12 :: x : 30, so 12x = 60 and x = 5 cups.
quiz.mistake: Adds 18 to 2 because 12 + 18 = 30

quiz.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 50,000. Two villages are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
quiz.explain: 6 cm on the map = 6 × 50,000 = 3,00,000 cm. 1 km = 1,00,000 cm, so that is 3 km.
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake converting cm to km

quiz.q: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the extremes a and d are 4 and 18, and the mean b is 6. What is the other mean c?
quiz.explain: Product of extremes = product of means: 4 × 18 = 6 × c, so 72 = 6c and c = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which numbers are extremes and which are means

quiz.q: Kabir mixes paint in the ratio 3 parts blue to 2 parts white. He uses 12 litres of blue. How much white does he need?
quiz.explain: Blue went from 3 to 12, that is ×4. So white is 2 × 4 = 8 litres.
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 to 2 because 3 + 9 = 12 (thinks additively)

quiz.q: Which set of numbers is in proportion, taken in the given order?
quiz.mistake: Looks for numbers that increase by the same amount

quiz.q: Aisha's photo is 4 cm wide and 6 cm tall. She enlarges it in proportion so it is 10 cm wide. How tall is it now?
quiz.explain: 4 : 6 :: 10 : h. So 4h = 60 and h = 15 cm. The photo was stretched 2.5 times.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 to both sides (4 + 6 = 10, so 6 + 6 = 12)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I check whether 2 : 5 and 6 : 15 are in proportion?
teach.praise: Multiply the outer numbers 2 × 15 and the inner numbers 5 × 6. Both are 30, so yes! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which numbers should you multiply together? What should be true about the two answers?

topics.title: Unitary method and sharing in a ratio

learn.hook: Is a ₹60 pack of 500 g biscuits a better deal than a ₹84 pack of 750 g? Find the price of the same amount and you will know!
points: Unitary method: first find the value of ONE unit, then multiply for as many units as you need.
5 kg of apples cost ₹600, so 1 kg costs ₹120 and 8 kg cost ₹960.
To compare deals, find the price per gram, per 100 g or per kg. The lower unit price is the better buy.
To divide an amount in the ratio a : b, add the parts (a + b), find one part, then multiply.
₹900 in the ratio 4 : 5: 9 parts, 1 part = ₹100, so the shares are ₹400 and ₹500.

example.q: 3 pens cost ₹45. What do 7 pens cost?

learn.reallife: Comparing prices at a market, splitting a taxi fare, or sharing prize money in a ratio all use the unitary method.

items.q: 4 kg rice cost ₹240. Cost of 1 kg?
A train goes 240 km in 4 hours. km in 1 hour?

games.title: Best buy first
games.prompt: Arrange from cheapest per kg to costliest per kg
items: 2 kg for ₹90
1 kg for ₹48
5 kg for ₹250
3 kg for ₹165
500 g for ₹30

quiz.q: 5 kg of apples cost ₹600. What do 8 kg cost?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the total price by 8 without finding the cost of 1 kg

quiz.q: ₹900 is divided between Riya and Arjun in the ratio 4 : 5. How much does Riya get?
quiz.explain: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. 1 part = ₹900 ÷ 9 = ₹100. Riya gets 4 parts = ₹400.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 4 or by 10 instead of by the total number of parts

quiz.q: A 500 g pack of biscuits costs ₹60 and a 750 g pack costs ₹84. Which is the better buy?
options: The 500 g pack, because it costs less money
The 500 g pack, at ₹12 per 100 g
The 750 g pack, at ₹11.20 per 100 g
quiz.explain: 500 g for ₹60 is ₹12 per 100 g. 750 g for ₹84 is ₹84 ÷ 7.5 = ₹11.20 per 100 g. The bigger pack is cheaper per gram.
quiz.mistake: Picks the pack with the lower total price instead of the lower unit price

quiz.q: A train covers 360 km in 6 hours at a steady speed. How far does it go in 4 hours?
quiz.explain: In 1 hour it covers 360 ÷ 6 = 60 km. In 4 hours it covers 4 × 60 = 240 km.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the distance for 1 hour, or divides by 4

quiz.q: Harpreet and Joseph share 42 laddoos in the ratio 3 : 4. How many does Joseph get?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 = 7 parts. 1 part = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 laddoos. Joseph gets 4 × 6 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Gives Harpreet's share (18) instead of Joseph's

quiz.q: 12 notebooks cost ₹540. What does one notebook cost?
quiz.explain: One notebook costs ₹540 ÷ 12 = ₹45.
quiz.mistake: Makes a division slip, for example 540 ÷ 10

quiz.q: A recipe needs 250 g of sugar for 4 people. How much sugar is needed for 10 people?
quiz.explain: For 1 person: 250 ÷ 4 = 62.5 g. For 10 people: 10 × 62.5 = 625 g.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 250 by 10 without first finding the amount for 1 person

quiz.q: ₹1200 is divided among three friends in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the largest share?
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts. 1 part = ₹1200 ÷ 6 = ₹200. The largest share is 3 parts = ₹600.
quiz.mistake: Divides equally by 3 friends (₹400 each)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 4 samosas cost ₹60. How do I find what 7 samosas cost?
teach.praise: First one samosa: ₹60 ÷ 4 = ₹15. Then 7 × ₹15 = ₹105. The unitary method is yummy!
teach.nudge: What should you find first, before working out 7 samosas?

topics.title: Mixtures and the rule of three

learn.hook: Indian mathematicians had a name for the method you use to scale recipes: trairāśika, the rule of three. It's over 1500 years old!
points: Compare strengths of mixtures by the fraction of the strong part. Coffee 1 : 3 (decoction : milk) has 1/4 decoction; 2 : 5 has 2/7 ≈ 0.29. So 2 : 5 is stronger.
Rule of three: if a gives b, then c gives d = b × c ÷ a. In Sanskrit: pramāṇa (a), phala (b), icchā (c) and icchāphala (d, the answer).
Change to the same units before setting up the proportion: if 500 g cost ₹30, then 2 kg = 2000 g cost 30 × 2000 ÷ 500 = ₹120.
The rule of three works only when the quantities grow together. If 4 workers take 6 days, 8 workers do NOT take 12 days — more workers take fewer days (3 days). These are inversely related.

example.q: 5 kg of rice costs ₹225. Use the rule of three to find the cost of 8 kg.
steps: pramāṇa a = 5 kg, phala b = ₹225, icchā c = 8 kg

learn.reallife: Chefs, pharmacists and paint mixers all use the rule of three every working day.

games.title: Rule of three works directly?
items: Cost and number of pens
Distance and time at steady speed
Sugar and number of laddoos
Workers and days to finish a job
Speed and time for a fixed trip
Pipes and time to fill a tank

quiz.q: Lemonade A has lemon juice : water = 2 : 5. Lemonade B has 3 : 8. Which is stronger?
quiz.explain: Compare the fraction of juice in each: A has 2/7, B has 3/11. 2/7 is slightly larger, so A is stronger.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the juice amounts, not the fractions

quiz.q: Coffee X has decoction : milk = 1 : 3. Coffee Y has 2 : 5. Which is stronger?
options: X, because it has less milk
quiz.explain: X is 1/4 = 0.25 decoction and Y is 2/7 ≈ 0.29 decoction, so Y is stronger.
quiz.mistake: Compares the milk amounts only

quiz.q: 5 kg of rice costs ₹225. What do 8 kg cost?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 to the cost because 3 kg were added

quiz.q: In the rule of three, what is the quantity we want to find the result for called?
quiz.explain: icchā means 'wish' — the quantity we want. Its result is icchāphala.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the four Sanskrit terms

quiz.q: 3 notebooks cost ₹48. Using the rule of three, what is the icchāphala for 10 notebooks?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 without dividing by 3

quiz.q: 250 g of cashews cost ₹240. What does 1.5 kg cost?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change kg into g first

quiz.q: 4 workers paint a wall in 6 days. Raju uses the rule of three and says 8 workers take 12 days. What is wrong?
options: More workers need fewer days, so the rule of three does not apply directly
quiz.explain: Workers and days are inversely related: twice the workers take half the time, 3 days.
quiz.mistake: Uses the rule of three for inverse quantities

quiz.q: 6 litres of paint cover 45 m². How much area does 1200 mL cover?
quiz.mistake: Treats 1200 mL as 1200 litres

teach.ask: Gappu's grandma says '2 kg of mangoes cost ₹180, so 5 kg cost...?' Teach Gappu the rule of three!
teach.praise: ₹180 ÷ 2 × 5 = ₹450! The ancient rule of three solved it in one line.
teach.nudge: What does 1 kg cost? Then how do you get 5 kg?

learn.hook: Asha puts ₹30,000 into a juice stall and Bilal puts ₹20,000. They earn ₹15,000. Is splitting it half-half fair?
points: Partners usually share profit in the ratio of their investments. Asha : Bilal = 30,000 : 20,000 = 3 : 2.
Split the profit using total parts: 3 + 2 = 5 parts, 1 part = 15,000 ÷ 5 = ₹3000. Asha gets ₹9000 and Bilal gets ₹6000.
In a mixture, find the amount of each part first. 20 L of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1 has 15 L milk and 5 L water.
To change the ratio by adding one part, keep the other part fixed. To make the 20 L mix 3 : 2, the 15 L milk needs 10 L water, so add 5 L water.

example.q: Divide a profit of ₹15,000 between Asha (₹30,000 invested) and Bilal (₹20,000).

learn.reallife: Family businesses and self-help groups in villages share earnings by contribution, just like this.

items.q: Milk in 20 L of milk : water = 3 : 1

games.title: Fix the mixture
items: Find the amount of each part now
Keep the part that is not added fixed
Use the new ratio to find the needed amount of the other part
Subtract to find how much to add

quiz.q: Ravi invests ₹40,000 and Sana invests ₹60,000. They share a profit of ₹25,000 by investment. What is Ravi's share?
quiz.mistake: Shares the profit equally

quiz.q: Three partners invest in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and earn ₹18,000. What is the largest share?
quiz.explain: 6 parts in all, 1 part = ₹3000, so the largest share is 3 × 3000 = ₹9000.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 partners instead of 6 parts

quiz.q: Meena invests ₹15,000 and Kiran invests ₹25,000. What is the ratio of their investments in simplest form?
quiz.mistake: Does not simplify, or reverses the order

quiz.q: Out of a profit of ₹20,000, partner A gets ₹8,000 and B gets the rest. What is A : B?
quiz.mistake: Compares A's share with the total

quiz.q: A 20 L mixture has milk : water = 3 : 1. How much milk is in it?
quiz.explain: 4 parts in all, so 1 part = 5 L. Milk = 3 × 5 = 15 L.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 instead of by the total 4 parts

quiz.q: How much water must be added to 20 L of milk : water = 3 : 1 to make the ratio 3 : 2?
quiz.explain: Milk stays 15 L. For 3 : 2, water must be 10 L. There are 5 L already, so add 5 L.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total water needed instead of the extra

quiz.q: 30 L of juice has concentrate : water = 1 : 4. How much concentrate must be added to make it 1 : 2?
quiz.explain: Now: 6 L concentrate, 24 L water. For 1 : 2 with 24 L water, concentrate must be 12 L, so add 6 L.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the wrong part fixed

quiz.q: 10 L of milk : water = 4 : 1 has 5 L of water added. What is the new ratio?
quiz.explain: Milk 8 L, water 2 L. After adding 5 L water: 8 : 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 5 L to the ratio numbers

teach.ask: Gappu and Pari built a stall. Gappu gave ₹200 and Pari gave ₹300. They earned ₹100. How should they share it fairly?
teach.praise: ₹40 for me and ₹60 for Pari — shared in the ratio of what we put in. Fair and square!
teach.nudge: What is the ratio of their investments? How many parts is that?

topics.title: Converting units: length, area and volume

learn.hook: A flat is advertised as 1000 sq ft. Is that bigger or smaller than 100 m²? Unit ratios decide!
points: Length units are linked by fixed ratios: 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 foot = 30.48 cm, 1 inch = 2.54 cm.
Area ratios are the squares of length ratios: 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm², and 1 m² ≈ 10.76 sq ft.
Land is measured in hectares and acres: 1 hectare = 10,000 m², and 1 acre ≈ 4047 m² (about 0.4 hectare).
Volume: 1 mL = 1 cc = 1 cm³, 1 L = 1000 mL, and 1 m³ = 1000 L.

example.q: Is 1000 sq ft bigger or smaller than 100 m²?
example.answer: 1000 sq ft is a little smaller

learn.reallife: Property ads, land records and medicine doses all need careful unit conversion.

quiz.q: Riya is 5 feet tall. Using 1 foot = 30.48 cm, how tall is she in cm?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: How many metres are there in 3.5 km?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 m in a km

quiz.q: A farm is 2.5 hectares. What is its area in m²?
quiz.explain: 1 hectare = 10,000 m², so 2.5 ha = 25,000 m².
quiz.mistake: Uses 1000 m² for a hectare

quiz.q: How many square centimetres make 1 square metre?
quiz.mistake: Uses the length ratio instead of squaring it

quiz.q: A room is 4 m by 3 m. Using 1 m² ≈ 10.76 sq ft, what is its area in square feet?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to convert, or converts only one side

quiz.q: Using 1 acre ≈ 4047 m², about how many m² is 2 acres?
quiz.mistake: Halves instead of doubling

quiz.q: Ananya drinks 750 mL of water, then another 1.5 L. How much has she drunk in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers without changing units

quiz.q: A water tank holds 2 m³. How many litres is that?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 L per m³

teach.ask: Gappu's uncle bought a 1-hectare field. Gappu wants to know how many square metres that is. Explain!
teach.praise: 1 hectare = 10,000 m² — like a square 100 m on each side. That's a big field for worms!
teach.nudge: How many square metres make one hectare? Picture a square field — how long is its side?

learn.hook: The weather app says 104 degrees! Should you panic? Only if it means °C — in °F it is just a hot Delhi summer day (40°C).
points: Celsius and Fahrenheit: F = (9/5) × C + 32 and C = (5/9) × (F − 32).
Key points: water freezes at 0°C = 32°F and boils at 100°C = 212°F. Body temperature is about 37°C = 98.6°F. At −40, both scales show the same number.
Word problems often need a conversion first. Manure at 50 kg per acre for 2.5 acres: 50 × 2.5 = 125 kg.
A tap filling 5 L per minute fills a 1.5 m³ tank (1500 L) in 1500 ÷ 5 = 300 minutes = 5 hours.
Metal content: a 5 g coin of an alloy that is 75% copper holds 3.75 g of copper.

example.q: Convert 40°C to °F.

learn.reallife: Doctors, cooks and farmers convert temperatures, volumes and land areas all the time.

quiz.q: Water boils at 100°C. What is this in degrees Fahrenheit?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add 32

quiz.q: A healthy body temperature is about 98.6°F. What is this in °C?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 32 but forgets to multiply by 5/9

quiz.q: Shimla's temperature is 25°C. What is it in °F?
quiz.mistake: Adds 32 without multiplying by 9/5

quiz.q: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same number?
quiz.mistake: Thinks 0°C is also 0°F

quiz.q: A farmer spreads 50 kg of manure per acre. How much does he need for 2.5 acres?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A tap fills 5 litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill a 1.5 m³ tank?
quiz.explain: 1.5 m³ = 1500 L, and 1500 ÷ 5 = 300 minutes (5 hours).
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 1 m³ = 1000 L

quiz.q: Each coin weighs 5 g and is made of an alloy that is 75% copper. How much copper is in 200 such coins?
quiz.explain: Copper per coin = 5 × 0.75 = 3.75 g. For 200 coins: 750 g.
quiz.mistake: Takes 75% of the number of coins instead of the weight

quiz.q: Fertiliser is used at 120 kg per hectare. How much is needed for a 5000 m² field?
quiz.mistake: Does not convert m² into hectares

teach.ask: Gappu's cousin in the USA says it is 86 degrees there. Gappu thinks that would cook him! How can you find it in °C?
teach.praise: 86 − 32 = 54, and 54 × 5/9 = 30°C. Just a warm day — no cooking!
teach.nudge: What do you subtract first? Then what do you multiply by?

learn.hook: A Diwali sale banner says '25% OFF'. That is just a fraction wearing a disguise: 25/100, which is one quarter off!
points: Per cent means 'per hundred'. 35% = 35/100 = 0.35.
To change a fraction to a percentage, multiply by 100: 3/4 = 3/4 × 100% = 75%, and 1/8 = 12.5%.
x% of a quantity = quantity × x/100. So 20% of ₹450 = ₹450 × 20/100 = ₹90.
What percentage is a of b? Work out a/b × 100. Getting 18 out of 24 is 18/24 × 100 = 75%.
Finding the whole: if 30% of a number is 45, the number is 45 × 100/30 = 150.

example.q: Kabir scored 42 out of 60 in a quiz. What percentage did he score?

learn.reallife: Marks in exams, battery levels on a phone, the chance of rain and interest in a bank are all shown as percentages.

quiz.q: What is 35% as a fraction in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 35% = 35/100. Divide top and bottom by 5 to get 7/20.
quiz.mistake: Simplifies wrongly or forgets that per cent means out of 100

quiz.q: Riya scored 42 out of 60 in a test. What percentage did she score?
quiz.mistake: Writes the marks scored as the percentage without dividing by the total

quiz.q: What is 20% of ₹450?
quiz.mistake: Finds 10% instead of 20%, or subtracts 20 from 450

quiz.q: Write 3/8 as a percentage.
quiz.mistake: Writes the decimal 0.375 with a % sign without multiplying by 100

quiz.q: In a school, 30% of the students come by bus. If 45 students come by bus, how many students are there in the school?
quiz.explain: 30% of the total is 45, so 1% is 45 ÷ 30 = 1.5 and 100% is 150.
quiz.mistake: Finds 30% of 45 (13.5) instead of the whole

quiz.q: Which of these has the largest value: 5/8, 0.6, 61%, 0.59?
quiz.explain: Turn all into decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 0.6, 61% = 0.61, 0.59. So 5/8 is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 61% is largest because 61 is a big number

quiz.q: A cricket team won 18 out of 24 matches and lost the rest. What percentage of matches did it lose?
quiz.mistake: Gives the winning percentage (75%) instead of the losing percentage

quiz.q: Meena spends 40% of her ₹500 pocket money on books. How much money is left?
quiz.explain: She spends 40% and keeps 60%. 60% of ₹500 = ₹300.
quiz.mistake: Gives the amount spent instead of the amount left

teach.ask: Gappu asks: What does 25% really mean? Is it 25 rupees?
teach.praise: 25% means 25 out of every 100, which is the fraction 25/100 = 1/4. Not always 25 rupees! Thanks!
teach.nudge: What does 'per cent' mean? Can you write 25% as a fraction?

topics.title: Percentages around us and in your head

learn.hook: Your body is about 60% water, a chips packet may be 35% fat, and 10% of anything is just one easy division away!
points: Percentages are everywhere: food labels (sugar 20% of the packet), the body (about 60% water) and surveys (45% of students prefer cricket).
Building blocks for mental maths: 10% = divide by 10; 5% = half of 10%; 20% = double 10%; 25% = one quarter; 1% = divide by 100.
Estimating a/b as a percent: 7/9 is a bit less than 8/10, about 78%; 5/7 is about 71%.
Bar model: draw a bar for 100% and split it into 10 equal parts of 10% each. Shade the parts you need.

example.q: Find 15% of ₹360 in your head.

learn.reallife: At a sale, '25% off on ₹1,200' is ₹300 off — a quarter — and you can work it out before reaching the counter.

quiz.q: What is 15% of ₹360?
quiz.mistake: Finds only 10%

quiz.q: What is 35% of 240?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra 5%

quiz.q: What is 5% of ₹1280?
quiz.explain: 10% is ₹128, so 5% is half of that: ₹64.
quiz.mistake: Stops at 10%

quiz.q: About what percentage is 7/9?
quiz.explain: 7 ÷ 9 = 0.777..., which is about 78%.
quiz.mistake: Treats 7/9 as 70% by looking at the 7 only

quiz.q: A bar for a 240 km trip is split into 10 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded. How many km is that?
quiz.explain: Each part is 10% = 24 km, so 3 parts = 30% = 72 km.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 3 parts as 30 km

quiz.q: About 60% of the human body is water. About how much water is in a 45 kg child?
quiz.mistake: Uses the 60 as kilograms

quiz.q: A 30 g snack packet label says sugar is 20% of the weight. How much sugar is in it?
quiz.mistake: Reads the percentage as grams

quiz.q: In a survey of 600 students, 45% prefer cricket. How many students is that?
quiz.mistake: Takes 45 as the number of students

teach.ask: Gappu needs 25% of 840 seeds for his garden but has no calculator. How can he work it out in his head?
teach.praise: 25% is a quarter: 840 ÷ 4 = 210. Halve, then halve again — easy!
teach.nudge: Which simple fraction is the same as 25%?

learn.hook: Your height grew from 140 cm to 147 cm and your little cousin's from 70 cm to 77 cm. Both grew 7 cm, but who grew more in percentage?
points: Percentage change = (change ÷ original value) × 100.
Always divide by the ORIGINAL (starting) value, not the new value.
Increase by r%: new value = original × (100 + r)/100. So ₹200 up by 10% = ₹200 × 1.1 = ₹220.
Decrease by r%: new value = original × (100 − r)/100. So ₹500 down by 20% = ₹500 × 0.8 = ₹400.
Up 10% then down 10% does NOT bring you back: 100 → 110 → 99.

example.q: A cricket bat's price rose from ₹800 to ₹1000. Find the percentage increase.

learn.reallife: News reports say things like 'petrol price up 5%' or 'school enrolment up 12%'. Percent change lets us compare fairly.

items.text: Going from 40 to 50 is a ___ increase
Going from 50 to 40 is a ___ decrease

games.title: Percent puzzles
items: Going from 40 to 50 and going from 50 to 40 are the same percentage change.
Increasing by 10% and then decreasing by 10% brings you back to the start.
A 100% increase means the amount doubles.
Adding 100% of the amount adds the whole amount again.
To increase a number by 25%, you can multiply it by 1.25.
A 50% decrease of ₹80 gives ₹40.
Half of 80 is 40.
Percentage change is found by dividing the change by the new value.
We always divide by the original value.

quiz.q: The price of a cricket bat rose from ₹800 to ₹1000. What is the percentage increase?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new price (200/1000 = 20%)

quiz.q: A village has 5000 people. The population grows by 8%. What is the new population?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 instead of 8%

quiz.q: A school bag costs ₹1200. Its price is reduced by 15%. What is the new price?
quiz.mistake: Gives only the reduction (₹180) or adds it

quiz.q: Aisha's marks went down from 60 to 45. What is the percentage decrease?
quiz.explain: Decrease = 15. Divide by the original 60: 15/60 = 1/4 = 25%.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new value 45 (gets 33 1/3%)

quiz.q: Start with 100. Increase it by 10%, then decrease the result by 10%. What is the final number?
quiz.explain: 100 + 10% = 110. Then 10% of 110 is 11, and 110 − 11 = 99. The second 10% is of a bigger number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two 10% changes cancel out

quiz.q: A train ticket costs ₹400 after a 25% increase. What was the original price?
quiz.explain: New price = 125% of original. So original = 400 × 100/125 = ₹320. Check: 25% of 320 = 80, and 320 + 80 = 400.
quiz.mistake: Takes 25% off ₹400 (gets ₹300), but the 25% was of the original price

quiz.q: A shop sold 250 boxes of diyas last Diwali and 400 boxes this Diwali. What is the percentage increase?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new value 400 (37.5%) or gives the increase itself

quiz.q: To decrease a price by 30%, you can multiply it by which number?
quiz.explain: After a 30% decrease, 70% of the price is left. 70% = 0.7.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 0.3, which gives the decrease instead of the new price

teach.ask: Gappu asks: Something went from 40 to 50. How do I find the percentage increase?
teach.praise: The change is 10, divide by the original 40, and multiply by 100: 25%. Perfect!
teach.nudge: First find how much it changed. Then which number do you divide by: 40 or 50?

learn.hook: A shopkeeper marks a kurta at ₹800, gives a 20% discount, and still makes a profit. How? It cost him only ₹500!
points: Cost price (CP) is what the seller paid. Selling price (SP) is what the buyer pays.
If SP > CP there is a profit: Profit = SP − CP. If CP > SP there is a loss: Loss = CP − SP.
Profit % and loss % are always worked out on the cost price: Profit % = Profit/CP × 100.
Marked price (MP) is the price on the tag. Discount = MP − SP, and discount % is worked out on the marked price.
After a discount of r%, SP = MP × (100 − r)/100.

example.q: A kurta costs the shopkeeper ₹500. He marks it at ₹800 and gives a 20% discount. Find the SP and the profit percentage.

learn.reallife: Festival sales, sabzi mandi bargains and school fete stalls all involve cost price, selling price and discounts.

games.title: Profit, loss or neither?
items: Bought for ₹60, sold for ₹60
Bought for ₹30, sold for ₹45
Bought for ₹90, sold for ₹70

quiz.q: Arjun buys a cycle for ₹3000 and sells it for ₹3600. What is his profit percentage?
quiz.mistake: Divides the profit by the selling price (gets 16 2/3%)

quiz.q: Meena buys a lamp for ₹450 and sells it for ₹360. What is her loss percentage?
quiz.mistake: Divides the loss by the selling price (gets 25%)

quiz.q: A saree marked at ₹2500 is sold at a 12% discount. What is the selling price?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts ₹12 instead of 12%, or gives only the discount

quiz.q: A shirt marked at ₹800 is sold for ₹680. What is the discount percentage?
quiz.mistake: Gives the discount in rupees as a percentage, or gives the percentage paid (85%)

quiz.q: A shopkeeper buys a toy for ₹200 and wants a profit of 25%. At what price should he sell it?
quiz.mistake: Adds ₹25 instead of 25%, or gives only the profit

quiz.q: On which price is the profit percentage calculated?
quiz.explain: Profit and loss percentages are always found on the cost price, the price the seller paid.
quiz.mistake: Uses the selling price as the base

quiz.q: A fruit seller buys 12 mangoes for ₹240 and sells them at ₹25 each. What is his total profit?
quiz.mistake: Gives the profit on one mango (₹5) instead of all 12

quiz.q: Kabir marks a bag at ₹1000 and gives a 20% discount. The bag cost him ₹640. What is his profit percentage?
quiz.mistake: Divides the profit by the marked price (gets 16%)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: I bought a toy for ₹100 and sold it for ₹120. How do I find my profit percentage?
teach.praise: Profit = ₹120 − ₹100 = ₹20, and 20 out of the cost ₹100 is 20%. I am a smart shopkeeper now!
teach.nudge: How much extra did you get? And which price do you compare it with?

learn.hook: A shop raises a price by 20% and then gives '20% off'. Do you pay the old price? No — you pay less, and the shop loses!
points: Percentages can be more than 100: 150% of 80 = 1.5 × 80 = 120. If a price becomes 2.5 times, the new price is 250% of the old (a 150% increase).
GST is added as a percentage of the price: ₹800 + 18% GST = 800 × 1.18 = ₹944.
Marking up by r% and then giving r% off ends below the start: 100 → 120 → 96 for r = 20. That is a 4% loss.
Area changes multiply: if each side of a square grows by 10%, the area becomes 1.1 × 1.1 = 1.21 times — a 21% increase, not 20%.
If length goes up 20% and breadth goes down 20%, the area becomes 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 times — a 4% decrease.

example.q: A shopkeeper buys a fan for ₹500, marks it up by 20%, and then gives 20% off. Profit or loss?

learn.reallife: Bills at restaurants and shops in India show GST separately — now you can check it yourself.

games.title: Tricky or true?
items: A 100% increase doubles a number.
Marking up by 25% and then giving 25% off gets back the cost price.
If each side of a square doubles, its area becomes 4 times.
300% of a number is 3 times the number.

quiz.q: What is 150% of 80?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a percentage cannot be more than 100

quiz.q: What is 250% of 60?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2.5 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A school bag costs ₹800 before GST. With 18% GST, what is the final price?
quiz.mistake: Adds ₹18 instead of 18%

quiz.q: A restaurant bill is ₹1200 before tax. With 5% GST, what is the total?
quiz.explain: 5% of 1200 = 60, so the total is ₹1260.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the tax

quiz.q: A shopkeeper buys a toy for ₹500, marks it up by 20%, then gives a 20% discount. How much money does he lose?
quiz.explain: Marked price ₹600; after 20% off, SP = ₹480. Loss = 500 − 480 = ₹20.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal percentages cancel out

quiz.q: A price is marked up by 25% and then reduced by 25%. What is the overall percentage loss?
quiz.explain: 1.25 × 0.75 = 0.9375, which is 93.75% of the original — a 6.25% loss.
quiz.mistake: Assumes +25% and −25% cancel

quiz.q: Each side of a square increases by 10%. By what percentage does its area increase?
quiz.explain: New area = 1.1 × 1.1 = 1.21 times the old, a 21% increase.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the percentage instead of multiplying the factors

quiz.q: A rectangle's length is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 20%. By what percentage does its area decrease?
quiz.explain: New area = 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 times the old, so it decreases by 4%.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two changes cancel

teach.ask: Gappu's shop marked a toy up by 10% and then gave 10% off. He thinks he is back where he started. Is he?
teach.praise: Oh no! 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, so I lost 1%. Percentages of different wholes don't cancel!
teach.nudge: Is 10% of the new price the same as 10% of the old price?

learn.hook: Put ₹1000 in a bank at 10% and leave it. With compound interest it is ₹1210 after 2 years — interest earns interest!
points: Simple interest is paid only on the original amount p: amount after t years = p(1 + rt). ₹5000 at 8% for 3 years: 5000 × 1.24 = ₹6200.
Compound interest adds each year's interest to the amount, so next year's interest is bigger: amount = p(1 + r)ᵗ. ₹5000 at 8% for 3 years: 5000 × 1.08³ ≈ ₹6298.56.
Depreciation (losing value) works by repeated multiplication too: a scooter worth ₹60,000 losing 10% a year is worth 60,000 × 0.9 × 0.9 = ₹48,600 after 2 years.
Populations and prices (inflation) grow the same way: 20,000 people growing 5% a year become 20,000 × 1.05² = 22,050 after 2 years.
Percentage share: a family spending ₹12,000 of ₹40,000 on food spends 30% on food.

example.q: Compare simple and compound interest on ₹1000 at 10% for 2 years.
steps: Compound gives ₹10 more (interest on the first year's interest)

learn.reallife: Bank fixed deposits, home loans and even the value of a used phone all follow these rules.

games.title: Grows or shrinks?
items: ₹1000 at 10% compound interest
Town of 20,000 growing 5% a year
Prices with 6% inflation
Car losing 15% value a year
Phone depreciating 20% a year
Pond water evaporating 10% a week

quiz.q: ₹2000 is deposited at 5% simple interest per year. What is the amount after 4 years?
quiz.explain: Interest = 2000 × 0.05 × 4 = ₹400, so the amount is ₹2400.
quiz.mistake: Uses compound growth or forgets to add the principal

quiz.q: ₹1000 is deposited at 10% compound interest per year. What is the amount after 2 years?
quiz.explain: 1000 × 1.1 = 1100 after year 1, and 1100 × 1.1 = 1210 after year 2.
quiz.mistake: Uses simple interest

quiz.q: For ₹1000 at 10% for 2 years, how much more does compound interest give than simple interest?
quiz.explain: Compound gives ₹1210, simple gives ₹1200. The extra ₹10 is 10% of the first year's ₹100 interest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks both kinds of interest are equal

quiz.q: A scooter worth ₹60,000 loses 10% of its value every year. What is it worth after 2 years?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 10% of the original price both years

quiz.q: A phone costing ₹20,000 depreciates by 20% each year. What is its value after 2 years?
quiz.mistake: Takes 40% off at once

quiz.q: A town of 20,000 people grows by 5% each year. What is its population after 2 years?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5% of the original each year

quiz.q: With 6% inflation, a ₹50 notebook will cost how much next year?
quiz.explain: 6% of 50 = 3, so the price becomes ₹53.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 rupees instead of 6%

quiz.q: A family earns ₹40,000 a month and spends ₹12,000 on food. What percentage is spent on food?
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round

teach.ask: Gappu's grandpa says compound interest is 'interest on interest'. What does that mean?
teach.praise: Each year's interest joins the money, so next year's interest is bigger. My savings will grow faster!
teach.nudge: What happens to the first year's interest in the second year?

topics.title: Using percentages to compare and check

learn.hook: Ravi got 45 out of 60. Sita got 38 out of 50. Who did better? Raw marks can fool you — percentages tell the truth.
points: To compare scores out of different totals, change each to a percentage: Ravi 45/60 = 75%, Sita 38/50 = 76%. Sita did slightly better.
From a ratio to percentages: boys : girls = 3 : 2 means boys are 3/5 = 60% and girls are 40%.
On ingredient labels, the parts add up to 100%: wheat 60%, sugar 25%, oil 12%, so everything else is 3%.
Check whether a claim can be true: in a class of 30, '40% are boys' means 12 boys. A claim of 35% of 30 people (10.5 people) cannot be exactly true.

example.q: Team A won 18 of 24 matches, Team B won 21 of 30. Which team has the better record?

learn.reallife: Board exam results, cricket strike rates and election results are compared using percentages.

games.title: Can it be exactly true for a class of 40?
items: 25% wear glasses
15% walk to school
60% like maths
12.5% have a dog
33% are left-handed
17% play chess
2% are twins

quiz.q: Ravi scored 45 out of 60 and Sita scored 38 out of 50. Who did better?
quiz.explain: 45/60 = 75% and 38/50 = 76%. Sita's percentage is higher.
quiz.mistake: Compares raw marks with different totals

quiz.q: Team A won 18 of 24 matches; Team B won 21 of 30. Which team has a better winning percentage?
quiz.explain: A: 75%, B: 70%. Team A is better even though it won fewer matches.
quiz.mistake: Compares the numbers of wins only

quiz.q: In a club, boys : girls = 3 : 2. What percentage of the club are boys?
quiz.explain: Boys are 3 out of every 5, and 3/5 = 60%.
quiz.mistake: Uses 3/2 or 3 out of 10

quiz.q: A drink is mixed as concentrate : water = 1 : 4. What percentage of the drink is concentrate?
quiz.explain: 1 part out of 5 is 1/5 = 20%.
